summary: Beaumont sits at roughly 2,600 feet elevation in the San Gorgonio Pass, which means it gets the warm, sun-drenched climate of inland Southern California — 9.9 hours of daily sunshine on average — but with noticeably cooler nights (lows around 54°F) than the valley floors below, thanks to mountain air funneling between the San Bernardino and San Jacinto ranges. That pass geography also makes Beaumont a textbook bedroom community: Interstate 10 is the lifeline, funneling commuters west toward Riverside, Ontario, and even Los Angeles, while local employment leans toward healthcare, retail, and distribution rather than a single dominant industry. The affordability math is striking by Southern California standards — a median home value of $464,000 against a median household income of $105,164 yields a price-to-income ratio around 4.4, which is tight but dramatically more accessible than coastal markets where that ratio doubles. The built environment is overwhelmingly post-2000 master-planned subdivisions that sprawl across hilly terrain with wide streets, cul-de-sacs, and pocket parks, but limited pedestrian connectivity between them; daily errands almost always involve a car. Nearby trails into the San Gorgonio Wilderness offer genuine mountain access within a short drive. Beaumont is essentially a place where the housing math pencils out precisely because you're trading proximity and walkability for space and sky.
